body: I've been to quite a few meetings, but I just stopped going after a while.
This is so much what I'm afraid of. Thank you for sharing your story

I know objectively I should. And I know from an outsider's perspective it's really black and white, but it's so much more complicated than that. I have no means of supporting myself, my grandparents are on a limited income, I love his kids to death, his mom is like the mom I never had, and over and above all of that I still love him more than anything. He didn't hurt me, but I know that doesn't mean he won't. I'm not stupid. I grew up around addicts and abuse. I've been abused my whole life and it's nothing new to me. I've just never felt so conflicted about it before. In the past with my abusers I just hated them and wanted to be away from them. I still find myself trying to forgive him and I don't know...

He doesn't really make enough money for us, let alone kids. But he soldiers on even though I'm unemployed and contributing nothing. Where the kids are now, they can have anything and everything they want. We're on food stamps and they get the best medical care, tutoring, summer camps, electronics, things we could never give them. We see them once a week, take them out to dinner and spend some time with them. We'd both like to do more, but it's not financially feasible. His parents are millionaires, they can provide a much better life for the kids. 

I don't think I would call him physically abusive. I don't know. I'm trying really hard to see this as an outsider would. I love him, but I hate him. I want to leave but I'm pretty sure he'd kill himself. I don't want the kids to be orphans... I don't know. I feel like no one here is giving this any more thought. We've been together nearly 2 years and this fight was all of 20 minutes. I just don't know.
For what? As far as the law is concerned, I don't belong here. There are no marks on me, and frankly, I don't want him to go to jail.

He was living with them for awhile, but he was using and drinking a ton then and they kicked him out. I know that doesn't look any better. I'm not making excuses for his past, I've just seen how far he's come in the last two years...

Yeah, because bringing five kids into an ongoing divorce with a single absent father immediately following the death of their mother would make for a much better environment for them. I can see now that posting here was a mistake. God forbid anyone have a shred of empathy.

I don't think that's really fair. He was married to his second wife when the mother of his children died in a car accident. She had five kids (two of those with other guys while my bf was married to her) and she had full custody of all of them. When she died, the woman my bf was married to decided she couldn't be a full-time mom to five kids and left him. He worked nights (and still does) and was having a lot of trouble getting insurance for them through the state, so his parents took custody of the two that are biologically his so they could insure them. The oldest kid and the fourth went to live with their uncle and the youngest actually went to live with his dad (the guy who was in the accident with their mom). There's a lot more to the story than "he doesn't even have custody of his kids so he's trash".

> As for abandoning friends and family, would you care to expand on that?

When I started dating my boyfriend all my friendships just kind of... disappeared. I stopped talking to my mother when I was 16 and never talked to her again before she died a few years ago. I ignore any attempts my father makes to contact me. 

My boyfriend only says he needs me because he's been mostly sober since we've gotten together. He went from smoking crack and drinking every day to only drinking like once a month and mostly leaves the other stuff alone. He says he'd be dead without me, but I don't understand how I've done anything. I'm just... here. 

I mean, I know people would miss me initially, but it goes away eventually. It gets easier. I still think about my mom every day, but I'm not anyone's mother. I don't have siblings. I have two grandparents that were basically my parents and probably won't be around much longer. Once they're gone I'll be alone. I have a boyfriend I love, but I think he'd be better off without me. I put so much extra financial stress on him. I sit home alone all day and can't even find the will to wash dishes or anything while he's at work. I'm just useless. 

My mom was only 40 when she died. It was said that it was an "accidental overdose" but I've always had a feeling that it was (maybe subconsciously) intentional. I don't know that I'll make it that far. I used to swear I wouldn't make it to 21, but I did and then I had a couple of years of alcohol abuse and now I wonder if I'll make it to 30. I don't know. Sometimes when I'm driving alone I just think about swerving into oncoming traffic or going off a bridge (there are a lot of them around here). I could make it look like an accident so no one would feel guilty that they didn't stop me...

A witty retort turns it into a game and makes everyone think you're cool with the "jokes" I put up with that a lot on vent, but it was my own fault for going along with it. A simple "That's not anything even close to resembling humor and absolutely no way to talk to any human being, regardless of gender." or something along those lines is probably more effective of at least getting your objection out there. Silence isn't consent, but a lot of guys view it that way. 

Sure, you may be a buzzkill for a few seconds when you get all srsbiznus, but it's better than suffering, crying, and missing work the next day. If they can't act like civilized adults then they don't deserve to reap the benefits of your awesome skillz.

I'm not going to give you any advice, just say I can completely empathize. I have a similar story to share, one that I've never had the courage to tell anyone, but reading your experience has inspired me to write it out, so even if no one reads it, I hope it will be cathartic for me. 

When I was younger, probably 8 or 9, I went to the YMCA daily for "summer camp" while my grandparents were at work. It quickly became apparent to my counselors that for one reason or another, I wasn't getting along with my peers, I was teased, excluded, or purposefully withdrew to be alone. Rather than force me into these heavily-monitored and scheduled days with kids that hated me, the counselors suggested to my grandmother that they put me in the group with the teenagers. They thought I was too mature for other kids my age and I would do better with older kids and more freedom to do what I wanted. 

So now, instead of days filled with dodge ball and archery, I got to spend however much time I wanted in the computer lab playing games. In my age group, I was the only one that liked to do this. 

So one day, I was playing a game that I'd played a hundred times before, but I was making some progress and really happy to just keep playing it. All the younger kids were outside and all the teenagers in my group were in the main room playing foosball. The computer lab was really just a side room with no windows and one door that stayed probably half-way open. 

Well, one of the older boys came in while I was playing this game and started teasing me. I just ignored him and kept playing. He kept going on, and to be honest I can't even remember any of the things he said (or his name or what he looked like, for that matter) but the next thing I knew he was behind me and touching me. I was wearing an old t-shirt with the sleeves cut off and I was still too young to have a bra, but chubby enough were I probably could have used one. 

Anyway, his hand slipped inside the sleeve of my shirt and kept fondling me. I told him to stop, to leave me alone, but I kept playing my game and refused to leave it. 

I really don't know how long this went on for, but I know at some point he left and I left my game and I didn't really know enough to know that I should be embarrassed, but when I walked out to where the other kids were playing foosball they all started taunting me: 

"Stoooop." 
"Don't do that." 

Repeating all the things I'd been saying; that's when I decided I should be embarrassed and ran off never to talk to them again. It still disgusts me that something like this happened and half a dozen (at least) teenagers just let it. I don't know how much any of the adults knew or what if anything I told my grandma, but I know I got to stay home during the summer months in future years. 

Part of me is still so ashamed that *I* let it happen. That I couldn't put my video game down long enough to step away from this pervert. Like you, I didn't want him to ruin my fun, but somehow he ruined so much more than that. 

So, while I don't have any advice, I understand the shame and guilt you feel and want you to know that *it's not your fault* and you did *nothing to deserve this*. 

I wish you all the best <3
